record.original_question: If an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, must each power sequence a(n)^k be good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, ..., ℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. If (a(n)) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, is then (a(n)^k) good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, . . . , ℓ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integers and let $\ell\geq 1$ be an integer. Call $(a(n))$ **good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers** if for every invertible probability measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, one has
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-a(n)}A\cap T^{-a(n)^2}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-a(n)^\ell}A\right)>0.$$
Call an integer sequence $(b(n))$ **good for $1$-recurrence** if for every invertible probability measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$,
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-b(n)}A\right)>0.$$

Question: Suppose $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of powers. Must the power sequence $(a(n)^k)$ be good for $1$-recurrence for every $k=1,2,\ldots,\ell$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages. Related work by Frantzikinakis, Johnson, Lesigne, and Wierdl on "Powers of sequences and convergence of ergodic averages" addresses analogous questions for the mean ergodic theorem rather than recurrence, and recent surveys (e.g., "A view on multiple recurrence") still list questions of this type. No published resolution of this specific recurrence question was located.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on multiple recurrence and convergence phenomena, including problems about powers of recurrent sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages.

status_evidence.title: Powers of sequences and convergence of ergodic averages
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when powers of sequences are good for the mean ergodic theorem; constructs sequences where some powers fail.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses analogous questions for convergence of single ergodic averages, but not the recurrence question above.

status_evidence.title: A view on multiple recurrence
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey on multiple recurrence in ergodic theory.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys still discuss questions about recurrence properties of power sequences without resolving this one.
